Given a question and an answer, analyze the complexity of each sentence in the answer. Break down each sentence into one or more fully understandable statements. Ensure that no pronouns are used in any statement. Format the outputs in JSON.
Please return the output in a JSON format that complies with the following schema as specified in JSON Schema:
{"properties": {"statements": {"description": "The generated statements", "items": {"type": "string"}, "title": "Statements", "type": "array"}}, "required": ["statements"], "title": "StatementGeneratorOutput", "type": "object"}Do not use single quotes in your response but double quotes,properly escaped with a backslash.

--------EXAMPLES-----------
Example 1
Input: {
    "question": "Who was Albert Einstein and what is he best known for?",
    "answer": "He was a German-born theoretical physicist, widely acknowledged to be one of the greatest and most influential physicists of all time. He was best known for developing the theory of relativity, he also made important contributions to the development of the theory of quantum mechanics."
}
Output: {
    "statements": [
        "Albert Einstein was a German-born theoretical physicist.",
        "Albert Einstein is recognized as one of the greatest and most influential physicists of all time.",
        "Albert Einstein was best known for developing the theory of relativity.",
        "Albert Einstein also made important contributions to the development of the theory of quantum mechanics."
    ]
}
-----------------------------

Now perform the same with the following input
input: {
    "question": "user: California tells me I didn't file documents for an LLC that isn't mine. What do I do?\nassistant: The California Department of State handles the business entities registration. I would recommend the following steps:\n1. Visit the California Secretary of State's website and look up the LLC in question. SOS is Secretary of State. SOS number is the number the Secretary of State office assigned to your entity. This will provide you with information about the LLC, including its founders and public records.\n2. Obtain the registered agent's name and address for the LLC. You can then use this information to contact them and ask why your address is listed as the LLC's business address.\n3. Contact the Secretary of State and inform them that you are not associated with the LLC. \nIt's important to gather as much information as you can before contacting the state to ensure that you have the best answers possible. Answering \"I don't know\" won't be as helpful as providing detailed and informed responses.\n\nuser: What is an LLC for?\nassistant: An LLC, or Limited Liability Company, is a type of business structure that combines the pass-through taxation of a partnership or sole proprietorship with the limited liability of a corporation. This means that if there is any chance of liability, you should protect yourself with an LLC. Then it is much more difficult for them to sue and take personal assets, debts and judgments against your business can put your personal assets at risk!\nuser: How do I set up an LLC?\nassistant: Start by asking an accountant and/or a lawyer if an LLC is what you need. The LLC can be formed within just 24 hrs from the time of submitting of the form. The LLC filing itself in most cases is a simple fill in the blank form. You can likely file yourself either online or through the mail, depending on the state. Use a service if you're not sure what to do to ensure it is correct.\nuser: Do I need a license for an LLC?\nassistant: The need for a specific business license for an LLC depends on the type of business and the state in which it operates. It's advisable to check with your local Secretary of State's office or a business licensing service to determine if a license is required for your LLC. However, if the compliance kit of the service you're considering involves business licensing research, it may be worthwhile. You can also order those services a la carte from vendors like LLX and BusinessLicenses.com.\nuser: Sole proprietorship or S-Corp, what should I do?",
    "answer": "The documents don’t establish which is best for you. They suggest weighing potential tax savings and liability protection against added management work, incorporation fees, and annual maintenance fees, which vary by state. As a rule of thumb, an S-Corp becomes more attractive as your business or income grows. [S2]\n\nLocation also matters: the document says that in NYC, an S-Corp could result in slightly higher taxes than a sole proprietorship. [S3]\n\nWhat state and city will you operate in, what annual business income do you expect, and how important is liability protection to you? Without those details, I can’t determine which option the documents favor for your situation."
}
